Question Choices: Select. Does $\{(3,4), (4,5), (5,6), (3,4)\}$ represent a function? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Each input must have exactly one output. Repeating an identical pair is allowed, and different inputs may share an output. A repeated input with different outputs fails.
Solution: For each input, collect its distinct outputs: 3 → 4; 4 → 5; 5 → 6. Every input has exactly one output, so this IS a function. Identical repeated pairs do not change it. Requested answer: Yes.

Question Choices: Select. Does $x = y^2$ define y as a function of x over the real numbers? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A relation defines y as a function of x only when each allowed x has exactly one y. A polynomial rule y=... gives one output, but x=y² permits both signs of y for positive x.
Solution: For x=4, both y=2 and y=−2 satisfy x=y², because 2²=(−2)²=4. Thus one input has two outputs; y is NOT a function of x with no sign restriction. Requested answer: No.

Question Choices: Select. Does a vertical line represent y as a function of x? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A graph represents y as a function of x when every vertical line meets it at most once. A horizontal line passes. A vertical line or a circle with positive radius fails because at least one x has multiple y-values.
Solution: A graph represents y as a function of x when every vertical line meets it at most once. A horizontal line passes. A vertical line or a circle with positive radius fails because at least one x has multiple y-values. A vertical line has infinite y-values for one x → not a function Requested answer: No.

Question Choices: Which is a function? "Student ID to Student Name" "Favorite Color to Student Name"
Hints: An ID belongs to exactly one student
Solution: One ID → one student is a function; one color can belong to many students

Question Choices: Which represents a function? "Day of the week to Temperature" "Temperature to Day of the week"
Hints: A day only has one official high temperature
Solution: Each day has one temperature; the reverse can repeat
